steps.title: What is email?
steps.body:
Email (electronic mail) is a way to send messages over the internet, like a letter but digital and usually delivered within seconds.

You need an email address for this, for example name@gmail.com. Anyone with an email address can send you messages.

steps.title: Opening your inbox
steps.body:
Open your email program (for example Gmail) through the browser or app. You will see your Inbox: a list of received messages. Unread messages are usually shown in bold.

Click on a message to open and read it.

steps.title: Writing a new message
steps.body:
Click the 'Compose' or 'New message' button. Fill in:

  • To: the recipient's email address
  • Subject: a short summary of what the message is about
  • Message: the text itself

Then click 'Send'.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Open your own mailbox below and try sending a test message to yourself. This way you'll see exactly how a sent message arrives.

steps.title: Note: staying safe by email
steps.body: Never open an attachment or link from a sender you don't know. Not sure? Feel free to ask the teacher via the Help button in the bottom right.

steps.title: What is an attachment?
steps.body: An attachment is a file (like a photo, document or PDF) that you send along with your email. You'll usually recognize the button by a paperclip icon 📎.

steps.title: Adding a file
steps.body:
1. Click the paperclip icon in your email
  2. Find the file on your computer or phone
  3. Click 'Open' or 'Select'
  4. Wait until the file has fully uploaded (you'll see a progress bar or checkmark)

steps.title: Large files
steps.body: Photos and videos can be large. For a too-large attachment, Gmail for example automatically offers a download link via Google Drive instead of a direct attachment.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Try opening a new message in your own mailbox and adding a photo as an attachment (without sending it).

steps.title: The browser
steps.body: A browser is the program you use to view websites, for example Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge or Safari. At the top you'll see the address bar: type a website address or a search term here.

steps.title: Searching the internet
steps.body: Type a question or search word in the address bar, for example 'weather today', and press Enter. You'll get a list of results. Click a blue title to open the page.

steps.title: Back and forward buttons
steps.body: Use the arrows in the top left (⬅️ ➡️) to go back to the previous page or forward again. Open a new tab with the plus sign (+) next to your current tab.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Search below for 'news today' and open an article that interests you.

steps.title: What is video calling?
steps.body: Video calling lets you see and hear each other over the internet, for example with WhatsApp, Google Meet or FaceTime. Great for seeing family who live far away!

steps.title: Camera and microphone
steps.body: Before you call, the app usually asks permission to use your camera and microphone. Click 'Allow' so the other person can see and hear you.

steps.title: Starting a call
steps.body:
1. Open the app (for example WhatsApp)
  2. Find the contact
  3. Click the video camera icon 📹
  4. Wait for the other person to answer

steps.title: Ending a call
steps.body: Click the red phone button to end the call. That's it!
